tests.why: Night glucose Aug 17/18/19 = 9.8 / 11.7 / 10.4, the three worst nights on record, consecutive. Morning tracks the night before. Aug 1 supper 6:30pm WITH sourdough and rhubarb crisp = 6.6 bedtime.
tests.success: Kitchen closes 6:30pm. If night readings fall under 8 within 7 days, timing is confirmed as the dominant lever.

tests.why: Whoosh on 5 of 9 sauerkraut days (Aug 11,12,14,17,18) vs 2 of the 8 days before it (Aug 3, Aug 9). Aug 18 was an isolated natural experiment: empty gut, only sauerkraut and coffee, big whoosh no warning. She pointed at it herself.
tests.success: 7-day pause. If episodes drop to 0-1, reintroduce and confirm. One variable only.

tests.why: De-duplicated dose by last committed value per session: Aug 9-16 ran 1300-1950mg/day, Aug 17/18/19 all ran 2600mg/day. Fasting rose over the same three days. Sustained 2600mg acetaminophen drains glutathione, which sits upstream of hepatic insulin sensitivity. Resting pulse also hit 82 on Aug 19, highest in record.
tests.success: If gait work drops the pain and the Tylenol falls back to 1300mg/day, fasting should follow without a diet change.
